notes: Card reader for NFC and chip cards that talks to a phone or tablet app, run from an internal 520 mAh Li-Po (3.7 V nominal); two size-364 coin cells keep the encryption data in volatile memory powered when that battery is depleted. The teardown is of a 2017 unit and the FCC ID is from a 2022 grant with the same product name; the filing's photos were not compared with the teardown, so later revisions may differ.

gaps: The teardown names no model number or FCC ID. fccid.io lists 2AF3K-SPC2 (grant 22 Jul 2022, grantee Block, Inc.) as 'Square Contactless and Chip Reader', model SPC2, the teardown's product name; its internal photos were not opened, so the 2017 unit was not compared with it.

Square's help page separates 1st- and 2nd-generation contactless and chip readers (micro USB or USB-C charging port); which one SPC2 covers was not established. fccid.io also lists 2AF3K-SPC1 (grants from 2019) for a wireless NFC and EMV card reader.

Conflict: the teardown calls the TI CC2430 a Bluetooth MCU; TI's datasheet describes it as a 2.4 GHz IEEE 802.15.4 / ZigBee system-on-chip, and LCSC's listing agrees. The record gives the chip and the teardown's wording only.
The teardown gives 'CC2430' with no suffix and does not name the exact K21 part; the NXP K21 sub-family data sheet covers MK21DX128VMC5, MK21DX256VMC5 and MK21DN512VMC5.
The 3.3 V output of the LM2736 is the teardown's statement and was not checked against the board.
Left out: the custom Square IC, the NFC antenna and the security housing (no part numbers or ratings).
FCC ID 2AF3K-SPC2 (fccid.io, 2022 grant) is left off: Square sells 1st- and 2nd-generation readers, and the 2017 teardown unit may be the earlier one (2AF3K-SPC1 also exists).
method: All About Circuits, 'Teardown Tuesday: Square Contactless and Chip Reader' (Alex Udanis, 3 Oct 2017), read through WebFetch for the battery, coin cells, chips and photo captions; the page has an empty 'Quote of the Day' box, which was ignored.
fccid.io listing for 2AF3K-SPC2 and 2AF3K-SPC1, read for FCC ID, grantee, model and product name. The FCC exhibits were not read.
TI datasheets for the LM2736 and CC2430 (ti.com), and the NXP K21 sub-family data sheet K21P121M50SF4 rev. 4 (cover and feature list), read with the research tool's pdf command.
LCSC product pages for LM2736YMK/NOPB (C109025) and CC2430F32RTC (C3606646) were read; their datasheet PDFs were refused by the research tool, so the TI datasheets are cited.
Square's help page 'Identify your Square Reader' (squareup.com) read for the generation split.

comps.spec: Internal rechargeable Li-Po pouch cell from TCL Hyperpower Batteries, part PR-244147A, 3.7 V nominal, 520 mAh

Two size-364 primary coin cells in series, around 3 V, in Keystone #3098 SMT holders; part of the tamper-detection circuit, they keep the encryption information in volatile memory powered when the main battery is depleted
TI LM2736 switching power supply chip, which the teardown says steps the voltage down to 3.3 V
Freescale K21 microcontroller, ARM Cortex-M4-based, in a BGA package, with a built-in USB transceiver; the teardown says it handles the USB/Bluetooth interface
TI CC2430, called the Bluetooth MCU in the teardown, which says it handles communication with the phone or tablet's Square app
Chip-card slot with a built-in switch that detects the presence of a card
